name: SQL/DS
tagline: IBM's first commercial SQL database (1981) for VM and VSE mainframes, built from System R; later DB2.
description: SQL/DS shipped in 1981 as IBM's first commercial relational database and one of the first SQL products on the market, running on the VM/CMS and DOS/VSE mainframe operating systems and built on technology from the System R research prototype. When IBM released DB2 for MVS shortly after, the two lines coexisted for years, and SQL/DS was eventually rebranded DB2 for VM and VSE. The line continued as DB2 Server for VSE & VM, whose Version 7.5 appeared in IBM's VM product matrix in 2007. Today it is mostly of historical interest, plus the odd remaining z/VM or z/VSE shop; new workloads belong on current Db2.
statusNote: The SQL/DS name was retired when IBM rebranded it DB2 for VM and VSE; the last major line, DB2 Server for VSE & VM 7.5, dates from 2007. Successor: IBM Db2.
strengths: Among the first commercially shipped SQL databases, proving relational ideas outside the lab
Brought System R's SQL, cost-based optimizer and GRANT/REVOKE security into a product
One code line served VM and VSE mainframe shops for decades
weaknesses: Only ran on IBM VM and VSE mainframe systems
Product name retired and no new major versions since 2007
Skills and tooling are scarce today
useCases: History of SQL and relational databases
Maintaining remaining z/VM or z/VSE applications
